newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel approves airwave auction bill.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel approves airwave auction bill.

text.p: The Senate Commerce Committee approved legislation covering federal airwave auctions that is considered less favorable to television broadcasters than a bill being considered in the House.
The legislation, intended to raise $26.3 billion under the budget accord struck between Congress and the White House, would bar the use of spectrum fees.

It also would extend the deadline for TV stations to return their analog licenses to the government if 95 percent of TV households do not have access to high-definition digital signals through such technology as cable TV, satellite TV and set-top converters.
That is considered less favorable for broadcasters than a bill that passed a key House panel last week.
That bill would allow broadcasters to keep their existing analog broadcast licenses beyond 2006 if 5 percent of their audience relies exclusively on existing over-the-air analog signals.
